problems: No tool failures other than nine URL_NOT_FOUND pages (listed); each was replaced by the nearest real title. Wikidata was unreachable: wikidata is null in all fifteen dossiers.
Fifteen dossiers were written, more than the 6-10 the brief asks for first; some used more than the 2-5 pages per state (Gujarat 8, Malwa 7, Gajapati 7, Reddi 6, Mewar 6).

Overlap risk with sa-05: the sa-05 scope text names 'the Rajput and Jat states', but Mewar and Marwar are in no sa-05 polities list; they are written here. guhilas-of-mewar (566-1303, another run) names kingdom-of-mewar as successor; no duplicate was found.
Slug mismatch: the sa-03 dossier eastern-ganga-kingdom names its successor 'suryavamsha-dynasty'; it should read gajapati-kingdom. This dossier's successor bhoi-dynasty is a guess.
Cliopatria konbaung-dynasty ends 1819; the Ahom ledger has the Burmese occupation of Assam 1822-1826 with konbaung-dynasty as occupier.

Sri Lanka: Cliopatria's Ceylon (1352-1506) and Portuguese Ceylon (1507-1686) are one-island rows that overlap Kotte, Sitawaka and Kandy; Portuguese Ceylon starts a century before the Kotte cession (27 May 1597); British Ceylon ends 1814 while Kandy falls in 1815. sa-06 owns portuguese-ceylon, dutch-ceylon and british-ceylon and should carry the matching entries. The overlap with Cliopatria's shapes has not been measured.

Mughal-empire is named as occupier of Gujarat (1535-36), Khandesh (1599-1601) and Mewar (1576-1585) and as gainer in several Marwar, Mewar and Ahom entries; the Mughal owner (sa-05) should carry the owner-side entries.
Several shapes depend on gazetteer names the gazetteer lacks (listed): the places resolve to 0 cells, so those shapes show only the districts and regions beside them.
Page-silent conflicts are recorded in each dossier's notes; six keyframes are intentionally empty (Malwa 1531-36 and 1542-54; Marwar 1571-82, 1679-80 and 1708-09; Kandy 1581-91).
musunuri-nayaks carries one validator warning: the ruler Prolaya Nayaka (1330-1332) predates the state's 1335 start.
